prompt: Write the lyrics of a country song about leaving a small town. Output only the lyrics.
raw:
**Dust in the Rearview**

*Verse 1*
Water tower's fading in the morning haze,
Same red light blinking like it has for days,
I packed my whole life in a half-ton bed,
With Mama's last words running through my head.
She said, "Baby, you were born with restless feet,
Ain't nothing for you here on Main Street."

*Chorus*
So I'm leaving with dust in the rearview,
A full tank of gas and a heart split in two,
Past the Friday night lights and the old church pew,
Every mile I'm gaining's one more thing I lose.
This town made me everything I am,
But it can't hold everything I am,
So goodbye to the only home I knew,
Just dust in the rearview.

*Verse 2*
There's the diner where I learned to drink it black,
The gravel lot behind the railroad track,
Where I kissed a girl who swore she'd never stay,
Funny how I'm the one who's driving away.
Daddy shook my hand, couldn't say a word,
But his eyes said more than I ever heard.

*Chorus*
So I'm leaving with dust in the rearview,
A full tank of gas and a heart split in two,
Past the Friday night lights and the old church pew,
Every mile I'm gaining's one more thing I lose.
This town made me everything I am,
But it can't hold everything I am,
So goodbye to the only home I knew,
Just dust in the rearview.

*Bridge*
They say you can't go back again,
But these roads are written on my skin,
Every cornfield, every creek, every name,
I'm taking you with me just the same.

*Final Chorus*
So I'm leaving with dust in the rearview,
Chasing down a dream I ain't sure will come true,
Past the county line sign, paint peeling blue,
Lord, I hope I'm doing what I'm meant to do.
This town made me everything I am,
And I'll carry it wherever I land,
So goodbye to the only home I knew,
Just dust in the rearview.

*Outro*
Water tower's gone now, sun's up high,
Didn't think I'd cry, but I guess I lied.
